title: One Point Lesson - Outlet Moisture Control & Retention Time (MT-2306) (OPL-YD-2301-06)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-YD-2301-06 - Outlet Moisture Control & Retention Time (MT-2306).

Equipment: YD-2301 (POLYMER FLUID BED DRYER), Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 2300 – POWDER DRYING SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-5500 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-2301.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
Outlet moisture control & retention time (mt-2306) for YD-2301 (POLYMER FLUID BED DRYER) in the POWDER DRYING SYSTEM. The product specification is below 300 ppm moisture. Rising outlet moisture means lost drying and off-spec powder.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Operating procedure & P&ID
- Tool 2: Radio / communication with panel
- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Read the MT-2306 outlet moisture every shift
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: If moisture rises above 300 ppm, check steam pressure PT-2304 first
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Verify drum speed and hence retention time is correct
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Cross-check against the daily lab moisture sample
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Adjust feed rate or steam to bring moisture back in spec
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Steam and powder leaking at YD-2301 discharge gland | Likely Cause: PTFE 4526L gland packing worn beyond service limit | Action: Replaced 8 pcs PTFE 4526L packing, staggered joints, re-nipped after
- Symptom: Minor powder weep at feed-end gland | Likely Cause: PTFE 4505L packing hardened and worn | Action: Renewed 2 pcs PTFE 4505L feed-end packing
- Symptom: Scheduled proof test of dryer outlet high-high temperature trip | Likely Cause: Set-point within tolerance, minor zero drift corrected | Action: Recalibrated TSHH-2301 to 125 degC and function tested to logic

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: The product specification is below 300 ppm moisture. Rising outlet moisture means lost drying and off-spec powder.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-5500: e.g. TSHH-2301 trips at > 125 degC - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-2301 before working on YD-2301.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
